sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate is deterministic-valid and faithfully encodes the static piecewise applicability rule: it targets ships, uses the canonical category classes, preserves the required thresholds and comparison directions, enforces the pleasure-yacht non-trade condition, uses the declared QUDT units and datatypes, requires exactly one category to prevent missing or ambiguous category evidence from passing, and compares the explicit boolean applicability result with the derived expectation. No vocabulary matching or further repair is required.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Use the canonical QUDT unit IRIs declared by the quantity metadata: http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M for lengthOverall and http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/UNITLESS for grossTonnage. The current qudt:M and qudt:UNITLESS expand to the QUDT schema namespace rather than the required unit vocabulary namespace. Preserve the existing ship target and applicability branches.

Replace the invented shipType string values "fishing_vessel", "pleasure_yacht", and "cargo_ship" with the supplied canonical ship-category representation, preferably RDF type checks against nltl:fishingVessel, nltl:pleasureYacht, and nltl:cargoShip. No verified controlled lexical values for nltl:shipType are supplied, so these literals cannot be assumed. Preserve the existing ship target, branch thresholds and directions, boolean applicability result, and canonical QUDT unit IRIs.

Reject accidental passes caused by missing or non-applicable ship-category evidence. The missing-input constraint only evaluates ships typed fishingVessel, pleasureYacht, or cargoShip, while the result constraint defaults to false when none of those types is present; thus a ship with no required ship type can pass with applicability false. Add a SHACL Core/SPARQL constraint requiring exactly one applicable canonical category representation for the supplied ship (and preserve the existing three branches), or otherwise ensure absent/ambiguous category evidence is a violation rather than a false applicability result. Do not activate the vocabulary matcher; all required canonical terms are already supplied.

The candidate is deterministic-valid and faithfully encodes the static piecewise applicability rule: it targets ships, uses the canonical category classes, preserves the required thresholds and comparison directions, enforces the pleasure-yacht non-trade condition, uses the declared QUDT units and datatypes, requires exactly one category to prevent missing or ambiguous category evidence from passing, and compares the explicit boolean applicability result with the derived expectation. No vocabulary matching or further repair is required.
